claims.text: As-cast WNbMoTaTi has a homogeneous coarse-grained or dendritic microstructure.
Annealing cast WNbMoTaTi at approximately 1100 °C for 30 minutes followed by rapid quenching will produce a dual-grain microstructure.
Rapid quenching can freeze the proposed dual-grain microstructure into WNbMoTaTi.
The treatment will preferentially form ultrafine grains along grain boundaries while retaining coarser grains in grain interiors.
An oxidation-free atmosphere and tightly controlled annealing time and temperature are required to prevent complete homogenization and obtain the dual-grain structure.
Ultrafine-grained regions provide high local strength.
Ultrafine grains increase yield strength through Hall–Petch strengthening because grain boundaries impede dislocation motion.
Coarse interior grains support ductility by permitting dislocation movement, dislocation storage, and strain accommodation.
Combining hard ultrafine-grained regions with soft coarse-grained regions can provide simultaneous high strength and ductility.
The annealed-and-quenched WNbMoTaTi alloy will have higher yield strength than the conventionally cast reference alloy.
The annealed-and-quenched WNbMoTaTi alloy will maintain or improve strain-to-failure relative to the reference alloy.
The proposed treatment should work in refractory high-entropy alloys of similar composition and processing history.
EBSD can be used to compare the grain structures of homogenized coarse-grained and grain-refined alloy conditions.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis predicts improved plasticity, whereas the predicted-outcome field allows plasticity merely to be maintained.

The predicted outcome allows maintained ductility, but the falsification rule requires statistically significant improvement in both yield strength and plasticity; a strength increase with unchanged ductility would therefore both satisfy the prediction and trigger falsification.

The reference state is inconsistently described as as-cast coarse-grained or dendritic, conventionally cast and homogenized, and conventionally cast without the dual-structure treatment. Homogenization can define a materially different baseline from an untreated as-cast alloy.
